text:
Sam Nguyen: Quick sync — region expansion plan for eu-west-3 + ap-southeast-2. Need to confirm routing policy, data-residency dependencies, and owners. TL;DR milestones: design by 3/24, infra readiness by 4/7, canary rollout 4/14. Who's owning what?

Anya Patel: I can own routing policy + canary routing rules. Need list of model variants we plan to serve there and expected qps per customer tier. Also: KMS keys and region-specific bucket names are required. :eyes:

Matt R.: For canary, prefer phased by customer tier (internal -> beta customers -> public). I'll own the canary orchestration if infra gives capacity. Question: any hard latency SLOs for these regions or just match existing region averages?

Jess K: Eng-infra here — capacity check: eu-west-3 has limited A100 capacity in our preferred zone. We can provision p4d-equivalent in neighboring AZ but that affects latency. Need exact vCPU/GPU count and target concurrency. Also need the model artifact sizes for pre-warm.

Sam Nguyen: Target first pass is the curated Llama-2-70B-int8 variant + a 13B for cheaper routes. QPS estimate: 400 steady tokens/sec (aggregate) for eu-west-3 during peak; ap-southeast-2 maybe 250. Those are rough. We should design with headroom 1.5x.

Anya Patel: Routing policy draft (example):
```yaml
route_policies:
  - region: eu-west-3
    priority: 10
    match: customer_region == 'EU' && model in ["llama-13b-int8","llama-70b-int8"]
    fallback: eu-west-1
    canary_percent: 5
  - region: ap-southeast-2
    priority: 20
    match: customer_region == 'APAC'
    fallback: sg-1
    canary_percent: 0
```
This is a starting point — need eng-runtime to validate compatibility with current smart-routing knobs.

Omar S.: Legal check — backups and async logs must stay within region for EU customers unless explicit consent. Who owns confirming S3 replication settings + backup retention? Security Bot, can you confirm?

Security Bot: Quick flag — cross-region backups default to disabled for EU-residency tagged tenants. But snapshots of underlying infra (host-level) might be replicated for DR — need to whitelist or change policy. Filing a ticket to compliance (RFC-7202) to confirm snapshot scope.

Jess K: Action item for infra: create a capacity plan doc with expected GPU types, instance counts, and cross-AZ network path. I'll draft by 3/28.

Matt R.: For runtime: do we support dynamic fallback to cheaper 13B variant when capacity constrained? If not, that's a feature request and could delay rollout. @Anya @Jess thoughts?

Anya Patel: We can add a fallback rule at routing layer to map 70B -> 13B if latency thresholds exceed X ms or queue depth > Y. Need metric hooks from runtime (queue depth, avg token latency) to drive it. Runtime team to confirm exposed metrics.

Sam Nguyen: Owners so far: routing policy + canary = Anya; canary orchestration = Matt; infra capacity + provisioning = Jess; legal/data residency = Omar + Security Bot; docs + GTM naming = Lina. I'll be overall PM. Deadlines: routing design v1 by 3/24, infra capacity doc by 3/28, KMS + bucket provisioning request by 4/3, compliance sign-off by 4/6, canary rollout 4/14.

Lina (GTM): Need region display names and any product caveats for docs page. Also need a short description of latency expectations for customers. I'll prepare a placeholder but need confirmed numbers by 4/1.

Matt R.: I'll queue a canary schedule draft and a prow job for canary traffic shaping. Expect initial canary window 48h for internal, extend to 7d for beta.

Omar S.: One more legal ask — data residency checklist: encryption at rest, customer-controlled KMS, no cross-region analytics exports. I'll send a checklist and mark required signoffs.

Devops Bot: [deployment pipeline] created region-expansion/eu-ap-sg pipeline (id: dp-9832). Auto-run disabled until capacity and KMS are provisioned.

Sam Nguyen: Blockers callout: 1) KMS key provisioning timeline (depends on security/compliance) 2) GPU capacity in eu-west-3 3) Runtime metric hooks for fallback. If any of those slip, move canary by 1 week.

Jess K: Agree. I'll prioritize capacity options and list a small set of acceptable instance families by 3/26. If EU capacity can't meet latency SLO, propose routing to eu-west-1 with traffic steering.

Anya Patel: Runtime owners — can you confirm metric endpoints by EOD 3/20 so I can wire the policy triggers? Also need a small test harness for simulated traffic (rps + token sizes).

Matt R.: Runtime: noted. We'll expose queue_depth and avg_token_latency metrics via /metrics with labels region/model by 3/22. Will add a synthetic load test harness (opens in CI) by 3/25.

Sam Nguyen: Great — next steps: Anya will post final routing yaml in this thread by 3/24, Jess posts infra capacity doc by 3/28, Matt posts canary schedule by 4/1, Omar posts legal checklist by 3/26, Lina posts docs placeholders by 4/1. I'll consolidate into a single project board. :thumbsup:

Jess K.: I'll ping infra procurement about reserved instances after capacity plan.

Lina (GTM): Adding action items to product-launch doc, tagging marketing for region announcements.

Sam Nguyen: Thanks all. If anyone hits a blocker earlier, drop a message here. Otherwise I'll follow up with a short weekly async status on 3/27.

Matt R.: 👍

Anya Patel: Thanks — will post the draft routing YAML and unit tests soon.
